tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
Pushes apart atoms that (almost) coincide, so that energy minimization can start.
Packed systems, such as membranes built with packmol-memgen, solvent boxes or molecules inserted into a solvated system, sometimes contain atoms of different residues that sit on top of each other (e.g. a hydrogen of one lipid tail 0.05 A from a carbon of another). The forces between them are not finite in single precision, and GROMACS minimization stops after a few steps ("the force on at least one atom is not finite") or crashes.
Every pair of atoms from **different residues** closer than the set distance (default 0.5 A) is pushed apart symmetrically along the line joining them to that distance; this is repeated until no such pair is left. Coincident atoms are separated along x. Typically a handful of atoms move by a few tenths of an Angstrom; minimization then removes the remaining strain.
Run it directly before energy minimization (and use its output as the reference structure of any position restraints that follow).
**What it does not change**
- Atoms of the same residue are never moved against each other, and bonded atoms of neighbouring residues are at least ~1.33 A apart, above the largest allowed distance (1.0 A). - Only the coordinates of moved atoms are rewritten; every other character of the file is kept.
**Outputs**
- The structure with overlaps relieved (GRO). - A report listing the overlapping pairs found (residue number, residue name, atom name and atom number), how many atoms moved and by how much, and the closest remaining pair.
.. class:: warningmark
This does not detect or fix *ring piercing* (e.g. a lipid tail threaded through a sterol or aromatic ring): there the atoms do not overlap, and minimization cannot untangle it.
